title: The stroke the day after Christmas 1969
summary: After Dance asks about the last years, the Jazz Fest in New Orleans in June 1969, Zutty describes waking with a numb foot and sensing a stroke after a fine family dinner.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Well, I think Zutty we've really covered the territory fairly well.
Well thank you.

Now there's one thing, I just wonder was whether you wanted to say a little bit about the last few years? You worked around New York with all these people like Wilbur DeParis, Tony Parenti (Dreher), Max Kaminsky and you went down to New Orleans in June '69 to play at the Jazz Fest?
That's right.
And then you had this stroke, when?
I had this stroke ....
Christmas, the day after Christmas.
And why was that? Had you been living it up Christmas Day?
No.
No? It just happened?
It just happened, yes. I got up and I was stretched out in front of the window you know, and I had my foot up on this stool something like

that. And when I got up and tried to walk and I walked in the front room, see, and so Marge asked me, what made you go in the front room? I say, I'm trying to wake my foot up. I said, it's asleep. And boy, it continued to get worse.
Oh thank you, Marge. That's fine, that's fine.
And I told Marge, I said I believe I have a stroke. And she said, oh, it can't be.
Why did you think that?
I don't know.
Did you feel it or something?
I felt like it was something like that.
We had had dinner the day before at his, at daughter's house.
Yes.
A nice time with the family. A big dinner and everything.
And that Friday night I.....
And he didn't get drunk or anything.
Yes because that Christmas fell on a Thursday I think it was.
Yes, because it........
Friday night, that's when I was straightening out you know, oh......
